messages.subject: PCA env (ecospat) - unclear parameters
parts:
Dear all,
Many thanks for your efforts regarding the use of MaxEnt and ecospat in a more familiar environment. However, when using ecospat within Wallace, there are some unclear parameters concerning some analyses, e.g. when using the functions ecospat.niche.overlap and ecospat.niche.dyn.index, it is unclear to what extent the resulting D and (BinOv, BinOv1⊃2 and BinOv2⊂1) are calculated.... and this is quite crucial. As you can see from the ecospat manual,

...the quantile of environmental density used to remove marginal climates. If intersection=NA, the analysis is performed on the whole environmental extent (native and invaded). If intersection=0, the analysis is performed at the intersection between native and invaded range. If intersection=0.05, the analysis is performed at the intersection of the 5th quantile of both native and invaded environmental densities...

So it is very important at what scale the analyses are carried out. The model guidance in Wallace does not give an answer.
I recommend adding this feature to the Ecospat module, along with the niche equivalency test, despite its controversy.
The second recommendation concerns the format of images/diagrams for export: is there a possibility to export in some kind of vector graphics? Or at least when exporting raw data, not only simple PCA results but full results could be downloaded for further analysis.
The last suggestion relates to the possibility of changing the colours of groups...

Thank you very much for considering my comments,
Best regards.
Martin

messages.author: 881c0dd9c7b0d196
messages.subject: Re: PCA env (ecospat) - unclear parameters
parts:
Hi Martin,
Thank you for your suggestions and feedback!

You are correct that the parameters for these two functions should be added to the guidance text. We are working on this now. For your reference, Wallace uses cor=TRUE for ecospat.niche.overlap() [from the ecospat guidance text: "Correct the occurrence densities of each species by the prevalence of the environments in their range (TRUE = yes, FALSE = no)"] and intersection=0 for ecospat.niche.dyn.index() [as you already wrote, "If intersection=NA, the analysis is performed on the whole environmental extent (native and invaded").

Also, the functionality for running a niche equivalency test is built into Wallace, but not included in the GUI (because as you mentioned, the controversy). If you wish to run this analysis, you can download your session code and edit the RMD.
The RMD will have the analyses separated by species (e.i., all of the analyses run for Species 1 first, followed by all of Species 2) followed by the analyses run with both. You'll find the section header ## ESPACE analysis for *Your Genus species 1* and *Your genus species 2* (Xx_Yy). You'll find subsections for PCA and occ density grid, and then in the third subsection you will see the niche overlap. The text mentions "Running equivalence test (FALSE) and similarity test TRUE", but you can edit the function to include "equivalency = TRUE". Add ecospat::ecospat.plot.overlap.test(espace_nicheOv_Xx_Yy$equiv, "D", "Equivalency test") to see the histogram. Note, according to the ecospat guidance text, the arguments for this function are the object, the type (Select the tested index. Must be “D”, “I”, “expansion”, “stability”, “unfilling”), and the title for the plot. Running your session code might be a good way to extract some of the raw data you were requesting that is currently not included for download in Wallace.
We can also add this information to the guidance text if it would be useful.

Bethany
The Wallace Team
